examples.text: Это я вчера специально выключил холодильник.
examples.trans: I was the one who unplugged the refrigerator on purpose yesterday.

examples.text: Абонент выключен! Какой кошмар!
examples.trans: The subscriber is switched off! What a nightmare!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('even') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Даже настоящий принц не такой королевский.
examples.trans: Even a real prince is not as royal as this.

examples.text: Даже не верится, я его не выключал!
examples.trans: I cannot even believe it, I did not unplug it!

examples.text: Даже ребёнок знает.
examples.trans: Even a child knows.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to believe'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Даже не верится, я его не выключал!
examples.trans: I cannot even believe it, I did not unplug it!

examples.text: Лев, важные гости уже ждут в зале.
examples.trans: Lev, the important guests are already waiting in the hall.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Я хочу, чтобы он от нас съехал.
examples.trans: I want him to move out of our place.

examples.text: Вика, я обещаю, он скоро съедет.
examples.trans: Vika, I promise he will move out soon.

examples.text: Ты обещал мне носки не разбрасывать.
examples.trans: You promised me not to scatter your socks.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (root 'ключать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to unplug'.

examples.text: Даже не верится, я его не выключал!
examples.trans: I cannot even believe it, I did not unplug it!

examples.text: Лев, важные гости уже ждут в зале.
examples.trans: Lev, the important guests are already waiting in the hall.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'from' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Я хочу, чтобы он от нас съехал.
examples.trans: I want him to move out of our place.

examples.text: Уже завтра он от нас съедет.
examples.trans: Already tomorrow he will move out of our place.

examples.text: От вас я этого никак не ожидала.
examples.trans: I did not expect this from you at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Вы что здесь делаете?
examples.trans: What are you doing here?

examples.text: Не думал, что вы так быстро вернётесь.
examples.trans: I did not think you would return so fast.

examples.text: Я хотел поговорить с вами лично.
examples.trans: I wanted to talk with you in person.

никак.gloss: in no way, not at all

meanings.en: in no way, not at all
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'in no way'.

examples.text: Ой, я сейчас никак не могу.
examples.trans: Oh, I cannot do that at all right now.

examples.text: От вас я этого никак не ожидала.
examples.trans: I did not expect this from you at all.

examples.text: Никак не могу.
examples.trans: I just can't.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to expect'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: От вас я этого никак не ожидала.
examples.trans: I did not expect this from you at all.

examples.text: Я не ожидал.
examples.trans: I didn't expect that.

examples.text: Мы ожидаем гостей.
examples.trans: We are expecting guests.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian num meaning 'twenty', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Двадцать тысяч я вычту из вашей зарплаты!
examples.trans: I will deduct twenty thousand from your salary!

examples.text: Я брала двадцать тысяч.
examples.trans: I borrowed twenty thousand.

examples.text: Ему двадцать лет.
examples.trans: He is twenty years old.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'thousand', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Здесь ровно шестьдесят тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: There are exactly sixty thousand rubles here.

examples.text: Двадцать тысяч я вычту из вашей зарплаты!
examples.trans: I will deduct twenty thousand from your salary!

examples.text: Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.

examples.trans: The town hall called me.

examples.trans: He's from Moscow.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович сейчас ваш прямой подчинённый.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich is now your direct subordinate.

examples.text: Уважаемые коллеги, прошу минуточку вашего внимания!
examples.trans: Dear colleagues, I ask for a minute of your attention!

examples.text: Да, теперь я ваш новый начальник.
examples.trans: Yes, now I am your new boss.

examples.text: В следующем месяце всем срежет зарплату.
examples.trans: Next month he will slash everyone's salary.
